title: BAE Systems Security Incident Stalls Notices From US Bankruptcy Courts
content_md: Federal bankruptcy courts across the US have been unable to send notices through the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) for a week. The outage followed a cybersecurity incident affecting the BAE Systems infrastructure that runs the center. The BNC handles notices for every federal bankruptcy court in the country, and BAE runs it as a contractor for the judiciary. On Thursday, the Administrative Office of the US Courts said that, because of the incident, the center is no longer generating or sending notices. “As a result of the incident, all access to the BNC systems and websites that BAE operates on behalf of the judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process are unavailable at this time,” the Administrative Office said . One of the affected services is the National Creditor Registration Service. While it is offline, users of the courts’ electronic filing system can’t generate the creditor mailing lists they normally use to serve documents. According to the US Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Texas, BAE first told the Administrative Office about the problem late on October 9. The disruption hit both BAE’s notice-processing systems and the BNC websites. Several bankruptcy courts posted notices on October 13, calling it a service disruption or interruption.
